newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soymeal ends mostly higher, most oil also up.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soymeal ends mostly higher, most oil also up.

text.p: Commercial buying and a late-session rally in soybean futures pushed soymeal futures higher on the close Thursday, floor traders said.
Soyoil futures ended mostly higher as well.
"Commericals were buying the meal and people think it is pricing," said one floor trader.

Commercial companies were active buyers in July soymeal following limit-down losses in that contract on Wednesday. After falling $10.00 per ton on Wednesday, the market reached a level that was attractive to end users, traders said.
The rally in old crop soybeans also pushed up prices.
Old crop soymeal export sales of 30,000 tonnes came in at the low end of trade expectations and capped gains in soymeal futures, traders said.
USDA put new crop soymeal sales for the week ended May 29 at 60,300 tonnes. Soyoil export sales were a meager 1,900 tonnes in old crop and nil in new crop, according to USDA data.
Soymeal ended $0.50 a ton lower to $3.10 higher, with July up $3.10 at $276.20 per ton. Soyoil settled 0.10 cent per lb lower to 0.18 higher, with July up 0.13 at 23.47 cents.
Rumors of Chinese interest in U.S. and South American soymeal soy also supported futures, but exporters in U.S. and Brazilian markets could not confirm any sales.
However, traders in Argentina said there were indications that China was actively buying soyoil, not soymeal.
On the day in soymeal, Term Commodities bought 1,000 bushels July and Continental Grain bought 400 lots August. Smith Barney sold 800 lots July, pit traders said.
In soyoil trade, Iowa Grain bought 300 lots July, 200 August and 100 December. Cargill bought 100 lots July and 300 December, traders said.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 36,000 lots, compared with Wednesday's actual volume of 44,920 lots. Soyoil volume was pegged at 22,000 lots, against Wednesday's 30,408 lots.
